title: Sentence pair
description: An aligned pair of sentences across two languages, used for translation utilities and future text AI. Content record — carries full governance metadata.

domain.description: Subject domain. Health, legal and civic pairs require specialised review and disclaimers before public or model use.

gloss.description:
A word-by-word reading of `source`, in source order.

Why this exists at all: a bare pair of strings teaches a model that two sentences correspond, and nothing about why. A gloss teaches which piece carries which meaning, which is the difference between a corpus that can be memorised and one that can be generalised from. It is the same reasoning that puts `forms` and `nounClass` on a lexical entry — structure recorded once beats structure re-inferred forever.

Optional, and expected to be absent on most pairs. Glossing is slow human work, and a pair without one is still a valid pair.

source.description: One token of the source sentence, as written.

gloss.description: What this token contributes. A grammatical label (DEF, PL, NEG) is as valid as a word, and is often the more useful answer.

note.description: Anything the label cannot carry — an idiomatic reading, a dialect remark, a doubt worth recording.

targetIndices.description: Which whitespace-separated tokens of `target.text` this source token corresponds to, zero-based. An array rather than a single index because alignment is genuinely many-to-many, and an empty array is a real answer: it says this token is not expressed as a separate word on the target side, which is exactly what happens to a definiteness marker translated into English `the`.
